pairing.title: A phone wants to connect
pairing.description: A device calling itself **{device}** is asking to connect, and shows the code **{code}**. Approve only if the same code is on its screen. Approving hands over this instance's chargers; the code is only for comparing.

user.title: What do you want to add?
user.description: A charger connects one physical charge point to SpotNav. A site is optional: it balances the load of every charger at one electrical connection under the main fuse.

charger_type.title: Choose charger type
charger_type.description: Automatic finds the charger's controls from its device: OCPP chargers and supported integrations (Easee, Wallbox, Zaptec, go-e, Peblar and more). Manual lets you choose any charge-control switch yourself.

resolve_vehicle.title: Resolve a detected vehicle
resolve_vehicle.description: One of these devices looks like a vehicle but reports more than one battery level, so SpotNav will not guess which one is the state of charge. Choose the device to resolve -- or choose the entry type again if there is nothing here you recognise.

resolve_vehicle_soc.title: Which reading is the state of charge?
resolve_vehicle_soc.description: Choose which of {name}'s battery readings is its actual state of charge -- or say that the device is not a vehicle you charge, so SpotNav stops reporting it.

ocpp_entities.title: Confirm charger controls
ocpp_entities.description: Only compatible entities belonging to the selected OCPP charger are shown.

data_description.charge_control: The switch that starts and stops charging on this connector.
data_description.current_limit: The charger's own current number; SpotNav only reads its value and range.
data_description.energy_register_entity: The connector's total energy sensor; it is found automatically, so leave it as it is.
data_description.current_control: Leave on "Do not set a current" unless the charger is known to accept the chosen method.

data_description.energy_register_entity: The charger's total energy sensor, used to count energy already delivered. Optional.
data_description.power_entity: A dumb charger behind a smart plug: the plug's power sensor (W or kW). SpotNav counts the energy from it and sees when the car has stopped drawing. The plug must be rated for the charger's continuous current. Optional.

site.title: Site
site.description: The site keeps its chargers' combined current under the main fuse. Active control can be switched on and off later; it is best effort, not a protective device. The main fuse rating must be entered explicitly -- it is never guessed from measured load. {charger_hint}

site_detected.title: Grid meter found
site_detected.description: SpotNav found these grid meters. Nothing is applied until you confirm; choose "manual" to pick entities yourself.

data.enable_disabled: Enable the disabled entities this meter needs

site_current_suggestions.title: Site current source suggestions
site_current_suggestions.description: These are only suggestions, based on entities already in Home Assistant -- nothing is applied until you confirm. Choose "manual" to pick entities yourself, or "skip" to configure this later via the site's options.

site_details.title: Measurement entities
site_details.description: Pick the grid meter's sensors. Any sensor is accepted; its unit is checked when you continue (current in A or mA, power in W or kW, voltage in V, reactive power in var or kvar, apparent power in VA or kVA). Only fields matching the chosen measurement source are shown. Each associated charger's phase wiring follows, one charger at a time.{charger_hint}

data.site_current_signed: The grid current is signed (export is negative)
data.derived_L1_power_export: L1 export power (optional, when import and export are separate)
data.derived_L2_power_export: L2 export power (optional, when import and export are separate)
data.derived_L3_power_export: L3 export power (optional, when import and export are separate)

charger_manual_source.title: Charger measured current
charger_manual_source.description: Pick one entity belonging to this charger's own device and name the attribute on it that holds each phase's current. Only entities registered on this charger are offered. Choose the unit those attributes report -- "A" or "mA" -- explicitly: an entity's own unit describes its state value, not necessarily unrelated attributes it also carries.

data.confirm_unverified: Nothing could be verified -- save anyway

site_manual_source.title: Site current from one entity
site_manual_source.description: Pick one entity that carries the whole site's current as its own per-phase attributes, and name the attribute holding each phase. Entities belonging to one of this site's chargers are never offered -- a charger's own sensor cannot also be the whole site's total. Choose the unit those attributes report -- "A" or "mA" -- explicitly: an entity's own unit describes its state value, not necessarily unrelated attributes it also carries.

data.confirm_unverified: Nothing could be verified -- save anyway

detect_device.title: Choose the charger device
detect_device.description: Pick the charger's device. SpotNav finds its controls from that integration's own entities; nothing is applied until you confirm the next step.

own_mode.title: Turn off the charger's own control
own_mode.description: This charger has its own smart, solar or load-balancing mode switched on: {modes}. Two controllers on one charger fight each other. Turn it off in the charger's own integration or app, then continue.

data.continue_anyway: Continue anyway (I accept that they may fight)

detected_entities.title: Confirm {device}
detected_entities.description: {warning}Found from the charger's device. Change or clear anything that is wrong. "Set the charger current" is off unless you choose it: SpotNav then writes the current only as the charger's write limits allow.{disabled}

data.energy_register_is_session: Use the per-session energy register (it resets each session)
data.charging_state_entity: Status sensor that says it is charging (optional)
data.enable_disabled_entities: Enable the useful entities that are disabled

ocpp_confirm.title: Charger found
ocpp_confirm.description:
Found this charger's controls. Continue to add it, or tick the box to change these choices.

{summary}

site_confirm.title: Site found
site_confirm.description:
Here is what SpotNav found for this site. Continue to create it, or tick the box to change these choices.

{summary}{charger_hint}

join_site.title: Add to site
join_site.description:
Add this charger to the site {site}?

{summary}

site_charger_wiring.title: Wiring for {charger}
site_charger_wiring.description: For a single-phase charger, choose the connected phase explicitly -- an unknown phase means no safe recommendation can ever be calculated for it. The charger's own measured current is optional: pick a discovered suggestion, enter one entity with per-phase attributes, enter three separate entities (one per phase, as the Charge Amps integration provides), or leave it as "skip" to configure it later.

charger_manual_entities.title: Charger measured current, one entity per phase
charger_manual_entities.description: Pick the sensor holding each phase's current. Only entities registered on this charger's own device are offered, and each must report amperes (A or mA).

charger_installation.title: The charger's phases, voltage between phases
charger_installation.description: The charger's entities do not say how many phases it charges on. Choose one phase or three: plans are figured from it. Where much of the network is IT (as in Norway) also say the voltage between phases; 230 V on an IT network, 400 V otherwise.

abort.already_configured: This charger or site is already set up.
abort.pairing_approved: Approved. The phone now holds this instance's chargers.
abort.pairing_denied: Denied. The phone was told, and nothing was handed over.
abort.pairing_request_expired: That pairing request has expired. Start again on the phone.
abort.no_supported_charger: No supported charger was found. Set up the charger's own integration first, or choose Manual.
abort.no_charge_control: No enabled OCPP charge-control switch was found for this device.
abort.no_pending_site: This site's details were not submitted before the manual charger entry was opened, so nothing was saved.
abort.no_ambiguous_vehicles: No detected vehicle needs resolving right now.
abort.vehicle_resolved: Vehicle resolved. Its state of charge will be read from the reading you chose.
abort.vehicle_dismissed: Vehicle dismissed. SpotNav will stop reporting it until it is undismissed.
abort.not_a_charger: That device is not an EV charger (a heater or outlet controller).
abort.charger_not_recognised: SpotNav does not know this integration. Choose Manual instead.
abort.charger_not_controllable: SpotNav cannot start or stop this charger. It can only be read.

error.safety_margin_at_or_above_fuse: The safety margin must be lower than the main fuse, or no current is left for the chargers.
error.charge_control_in_use: This charge control is already used by another SpotNav charger.
error.current_limit_in_use: This charging current control is already used by another SpotNav charger.
error.duplicate_charger: {other} and this charger are the same physical charger. Two SpotNav chargers on one charger send it conflicting commands, so keep only one: remove the other in Settings → Devices & services → SpotNav. SpotNav never removes one for you.
error.charger_already_in_another_site: One of these chargers is already assigned to a different site.
error.manual_source_entity_invalid: Choose a sensor entity that exists in Home Assistant.
error.manual_source_entity_wrong_device: That entity is not registered on this charger's own device, so it cannot be this charger's measured current.
error.site_manual_source_entity_on_charger_dev: That entity belongs to one of this site's chargers, so it cannot be the site's own total current.
error.manual_source_attributes_required: Enter the attribute name for this phase.
error.manual_source_unverified: Nothing on this entity currently matches those attribute names, and nothing in the last {lookback_days} days of history does either -- this may be a brand-new charger, or a typo. Tick "save anyway" to store it regardless.
error.own_mode_active: The charger's own control is still on. Turn it off, or choose to continue anyway.
error.control_path_unknown: SpotNav cannot tell how to start and stop a charge with this entity. Choose the charger's switch, or a select with clear start and stop options.
error.current_limit_required: Choose the charging current number to set it through.
error.current_control_unsupported: This way of setting the current does not fit this charger.
error.charger_no_answer: The charger did not answer, so SpotNav cannot tell how its current is set. Wait until it is connected and submit again, or choose yourself.
error.unit_expected_current: This sensor must report current in A or mA.
error.unit_expected_power: This sensor must report power in W or kW.
error.unit_expected_voltage: This sensor must report voltage in V.
error.unit_expected_reactive_power: This sensor must report reactive power in var or kvar.
error.unit_expected_apparent_power: This sensor must report apparent power in VA or kVA.
error.manual_entities_duplicate: Each phase needs its own entity.

data_description.idle_power_w: Below this power for five minutes during a planned charge, SpotNav says the car is not drawing. Default 100 W.

site_init.title: Site capacity settings
site_init.description: Load balancing under the main fuse. Active control lowers a charger's current when needed; it is best effort, not a protective device. The battery power sensor is optional and only feeds a diagnostic estimate -- never a safe charging limit.

data.name: Site name
data.active_control_enabled: Active control enabled (opt-in, derived mode only)
data.regulator_deadband_a: Active control: ignore changes smaller than (A)
data.regulator_dwell_s: Active control: how long a change must hold (seconds)
data.yield_stepping_enabled: Yield-verified stepping enabled (opt-in, for a site with a load that yields, e.g. a house battery)
data.yield_ceiling_a: Yield stepping: hard ceiling, never exceeded (A, must be greater than the main fuse)
data.solar_priority: Solar surplus priority (car or the house battery first)
data.battery_aggregate_power_entity: Home battery charging power (optional, diagnostic only)
data.solar_forecast_entries: Solar forecast sources (optional, used by the hybrid strategy)

options.derived_phase_current: Derived from power and voltage (more exact with the meter's current, apparent or reactive power; otherwise the current is estimated)

state.hybrid: Cheapest hours, holding back grid energy for expected sun

vehicle_soc_needs_decision.title: A vehicle's state of charge needs a decision

abort.no_longer_needs_decision: This device no longer needs a decision.

pick.title: Which reading is the state of charge?
pick.description: **{device}** reports more than one battery reading, so SpotNav will not guess which one is the state of charge. Choose the reading that is, or say that this is not a vehicle, which stops it being reported.

vehicle_charge_limit_needs_decision.title: A vehicle's charge limit needs a decision

abort.no_longer_needs_decision: This device no longer needs a decision.

pick.title: Which limit should a change set?
pick.description: **{device}** reports more than one charge limit, so SpotNav will not guess which one a change should set. Choose the limit this vehicle's changes should use. It is written through the vehicle's own integration, and takes effect when that integration next reads it.

duplicate_charger.title: Two SpotNav chargers are the same charger
duplicate_charger.description: **{charger}** and **{other}** are the same physical charger: they share a device, a measured current, an OCPP connector or an Easee device. Two SpotNav chargers on one charger send it conflicting commands. Remove one of them: Settings → Devices & services → SpotNav → the entry's menu → Delete. SpotNav never removes one for you.

site_without_chargers.title: Add a charger to the site
site_without_chargers.description: The site **{site}** has no charger yet. Add a charger: Settings → Devices & services → SpotNav → Add entry → Charger; it will offer to join this site.

invalid_driver.message: That energy source is not supported.

invalid_area.message: Select a market first: that value belongs to one.

invalid_amps.message: The current must be a whole number of amperes.

invalid_energy.message: The energy must be a positive number of kWh.

invalid_periods.message: The number of periods must be a whole number from 1 to 8.

invalid_departure.message: The departure must be a local wall-clock time.

invalid_fiscal.message: That fiscal value cannot be stored as it stands.

invalid_number.message: That value must be a valid number.

unknown_field.message: This record carries a field this version does not know.

missing_field.message: This record is missing a field it must carry.

invalid_proposal.message: That stored proposal cannot be used.

invalid_pause.message: The pause flag must be on or off.

revision_conflict.message: These settings changed elsewhere, so the value was not written. Try again.

not_auto_mode.message: Auto price is not the planning mode for this charger.

unknown_test_charger.message: No loaded SpotNav charger has that config entry or entity id.

no_push_registered.message: No SpotNav charger has the app's instant notifications turned on, so no test push was sent. Any Companion phones chosen for notifications were still sent a test message.

stop_not_executed.message: The charger did not take the stop: its control is unavailable. Try again when the charger is back.

storage_failed.message: The charging plan could not be saved.

reschedule_failed.message: The charging plan could not be armed; the previous one stands.

rollback_failed.message: The charging plan could not be armed, nor the previous one restored.

vehicle_not_connected.message: No car is plugged in, so there is nothing to start.

reconcile_failed.message: The charger took the command, but automatic charging could not be updated to match. Check the charger's status.
